questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver is leaving a stop sign in a fully loaded tractor-trailer on a flat road. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct way to apply power for a smooth, controlled start?

answers.text: Press the accelerator firmly to load the drivetrain quickly
Pop the clutch to engage maximum torque immediately
Apply power smoothly so the vehicle moves forward without jerking
Slip the clutch heavily until the engine reaches governed rpm

explanations.a: Firm or rough acceleration can break drive-wheel traction, especially on slick surfaces, and is not the manual's recommended method.
explanations.b: Popping the clutch loads the drivetrain abruptly and can damage the clutch, transmission, and driveline.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to accelerate smoothly so the vehicle moves forward without jerking, protecting cargo, drivetrain, and traction.
explanations.d: Excessive clutch slipping wears the friction disc rapidly and is not the proper starting technique.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual emphasizes a specific hand position on the steering wheel during normal driving and emergencies. Which grip does it recommend at all times for proper vehicle control?

answers.text: Both hands firmly on the wheel, on opposite sides, at all times
One hand at the bottom of the wheel for relaxed cruising
Both hands palms-down on top of the wheel
One hand on the wheel, one on the gear shift, ready to downshift

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to keep both hands firmly on the wheel on opposite sides so they can react to a tire failure or emergency steering input without the wheel being twisted out of their hands.
explanations.b: A one-handed bottom grip provides little leverage and cannot resist a sudden steering input from a blowout or pothole.
explanations.c: Both hands together on top of the wheel reduces leverage on either side and is not the recommended grip.
explanations.d: Riding one hand on the shifter leaves only one hand to control steering and conflicts with the manual's two-handed rule.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver approaches a red light at moderate speed in a heavy combination vehicle. What is the manual's preferred braking technique to bring the vehicle to a smooth, safe stop?

answers.text: Hold the brake pedal at maximum pressure until the vehicle stops
Apply steady, controlled pressure on the brake pedal so the vehicle stops smoothly
Pump the brakes rapidly all the way to the stop
Coast in neutral and rely entirely on the parking brake

explanations.a: Maximum, locked-on pressure can lock wheels, cause skids, and is not the controlled stop the manual describes.
explanations.b: Steady, controlled brake-pedal pressure delivers a smooth stop, keeps cargo secure, and keeps wheels rolling.
explanations.c: Rapid pumping is not the routine stopping technique; it is associated only with certain non-ABS hydraulic-failure recovery moves.
explanations.d: Coasting in neutral robs the driver of engine braking and is unsafe for routine stops.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver must back a tractor-trailer into a tight loading bay. According to the CDL manual, which combination of techniques offers the safest backing operation?

answers.text: Back at moderate highway-style speed to keep momentum through the dock
Steer with one hand and look only through the right mirror
Back blind and rely on hazard flashers to warn bystanders
Back slowly, use both mirrors, and use a helper to spot blind areas whenever possible

explanations.a: Speed compounds errors during backing; the manual specifies slow, controlled backing.
explanations.b: Single-mirror backing leaves the opposite blind side unmonitored and is unsafe for tight bays.
explanations.c: Backing blind without a spotter ignores the manual's clear instruction to use a helper when one is available.
explanations.d: The manual prescribes backing slowly, using both mirrors, and using a helper when one is available because this combination minimizes blind-spot risk.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.2 Visual search, mirrors, and following distance
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a specific minimum time interval that drivers should look ahead while driving. About how far ahead, in seconds, should a CDL driver scan?

answers.text: At least 12 to 15 seconds ahead
At least 3 to 5 seconds ahead
At least 30 to 40 seconds ahead
Only as far as the headlights illuminate, regardless of conditions

explanations.a: The manual states a driver should look 12 to 15 seconds ahead, which is roughly a quarter mile at highway speed and one block in city driving.
explanations.b: Three to five seconds is far too short and would correspond to only a few hundred feet at highway speed.
explanations.c: Thirty to forty seconds is much further than the manual's stated guidance for routine scanning.
explanations.d: Sight-distance braking applies at night, but the routine forward-scan guideline is given in seconds, not lighting range.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.2 Visual search, mirrors, and following distance
questions.text: Under 40 mph and on dry pavement, the CDL manual gives a per-length rule of thumb for safe following distance behind another vehicle. What is that rule?

answers.text: One second of following distance for every 5 feet of vehicle length
One second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length
Two seconds of following distance regardless of vehicle length
Three seconds of following distance for any speed under 50 mph

explanations.a: Five-feet-per-second is too short and would not provide enough buffer for a heavy CMV under 40 mph.
explanations.b: The CDL manual specifies at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph.
explanations.c: A flat two-second rule is for passenger cars, not the length-based commercial-vehicle rule.
explanations.d: The three-second guidance is not the manual's standard, and the rule is keyed to vehicle length, not just speed.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.2 Visual search, mirrors, and following distance
questions.text: A driver is operating a 60-foot tractor-trailer at 55 mph on dry pavement. Using the CDL manual's per-length following-distance rule with the high-speed adjustment, what minimum following distance applies?

answers.text: 4 seconds total
5 seconds total
7 seconds total
10 seconds total

explanations.a: Four seconds matches a 40-foot vehicle under 40 mph, not a 60-foot vehicle at 55 mph.
explanations.b: Five seconds matches a 40-foot vehicle above 40 mph, not a 60-foot rig.
explanations.c: At 60 feet of length, the under-40 rule yields 6 seconds, plus 1 additional second for travel over 40 mph, equaling 7 seconds total.
explanations.d: Ten seconds is more than the manual prescribes and is not the standard answer for these conditions.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.2 Visual search, mirrors, and following distance
questions.text: Mirror checks are a key part of safe CMV operation. According to the CDL manual's guidance on visual search, which statement best describes how a driver should use the mirrors during ordinary highway operation?

answers.text: Check mirrors only when changing lanes, since constant checking distracts from the road ahead
Stare at one mirror for several seconds at a time to spot all hazards behind
Use only the spot mirror for the right side because the flat mirror gives a misleading view
Scan all mirrors regularly with brief, frequent glances to keep aware of what is happening on all sides

explanations.a: The manual recommends regular mirror checks, not only at lane changes, because traffic situations behind and beside the vehicle change constantly.
explanations.b: Staring at any one mirror takes the driver's attention off the forward scene, which is the opposite of the manual's guidance.
explanations.c: Both flat and convex mirrors serve different purposes, and the manual instructs drivers to use both.
explanations.d: The manual instructs drivers to scan mirrors regularly with brief, frequent glances so the area to the sides and rear of the vehicle is constantly monitored.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: Signaling intentions early helps other drivers respond safely to a CMV. According to the CDL manual, when should a driver activate the turn signal before making a turn?

answers.text: Just as the steering wheel begins to turn
Only after entering the turn lane
Only when other vehicles are clearly visible behind
Well in advance of the turn so other drivers have time to react

explanations.a: Signaling at the moment of turning gives other drivers no warning and defeats the purpose of the signal.
explanations.b: Signaling only after entering the turn lane is too late for traffic that could not anticipate the lane change.
explanations.c: Signaling depends on intent to turn, not on whether the driver sees other vehicles in mirrors.
explanations.d: The manual instructs drivers to signal well in advance of the turn so others have time to react and adjust.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: Horn use is addressed in the CDL manual's section on communicating with other road users. Which statement best summarizes the manual's guidance on when to use the horn?

answers.text: Use the horn when needed to alert others to your presence, but do not use it unnecessarily because it can startle people
Sound the horn continuously while passing any slower vehicle
Use the horn aggressively to motivate slow drivers to move faster
Never use the horn under any circumstance because it constitutes an act of road rage

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to use the horn when needed to avoid a crash but warns that unnecessary horn use can startle others and create danger.
explanations.b: Continuous horn use during routine passing is not appropriate and can startle other drivers.
explanations.c: The manual specifically discourages aggressive horn use to pressure other drivers.
explanations.d: A blanket prohibition contradicts the manual; the horn is an important warning device when used appropriately.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: In addition to seeing the road, headlights help others see the CMV. Beyond night driving, in which condition does the CDL manual recommend turning on headlights to improve being seen?

answers.text: Only between dusk and dawn, never during daylight hours
In rain, fog, snow, and any other low-visibility condition during the day
On city streets only, where pedestrians are present
Only when the windshield wipers fail to clear the glass

explanations.a: The manual encourages headlight use whenever it improves visibility to others, not only at night.
explanations.b: The manual instructs drivers to turn on headlights in any low-visibility condition such as rain, fog, or snow so the vehicle is more visible to others.
explanations.c: Headlight use is tied to visibility conditions, not the type of road.
explanations.d: Headlight use is not contingent on wiper failure; it is a general low-visibility practice.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver is forced to stop on the shoulder of a divided four-lane highway during the day. Federal regulations under 49 CFR 392.22 require warning devices to be placed within a specific time and at specific distances. Which placement matches the federal standard for a stopped CMV on a divided highway?

answers.text: One triangle at the rear bumper and two at the front, all within 50 feet
All three triangles in a single line directly behind the vehicle, 25 feet apart
One triangle within 10 feet of the rear, one about 100 feet behind, and one about 200 feet behind on the traffic side
Only flares; reflective triangles are not authorized for divided highways

explanations.a: The federal placement requires triangles to the rear of the stopped vehicle on a divided highway, not in front of it.
explanations.b: All three triangles cannot be in a single line at 25-foot spacing; the federal pattern uses 10-foot, 100-foot, and 200-foot positions.
explanations.c: On a divided highway, 49 CFR 392.22 requires warning devices placed within 10 feet of the rear, about 100 feet behind, and about 200 feet behind on the traffic side, all within 10 minutes of stopping.
explanations.d: Reflective triangles are an authorized warning device, and the federal regulation gives a triangle-based placement pattern.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual breaks total stopping distance into three component distances. Which set of three components correctly sums to total stopping distance?

answers.text: Perception distance plus reaction distance plus braking distance
Drift distance plus skid distance plus residual distance
Approach distance plus following distance plus impact distance
Sight distance plus warning distance plus stopping distance

explanations.a: The manual defines total stopping distance as the sum of perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance.
explanations.b: These are not terms used in the CDL manual's stopping-distance breakdown.
explanations.c: Following distance is a space-management concept, not a component of stopping distance.
explanations.d: Sight distance and warning distance are not components in the manual's three-part stopping-distance equation.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual provides a typical perception time and the corresponding distance traveled at 55 mph. According to the manual, the average alert driver's perception time of about 1.75 seconds equates to roughly how many feet at 55 mph?

answers.text: Approximately 61 feet
Approximately 142 feet
Approximately 216 feet
Approximately 419 feet

explanations.a: 61 feet is the manual's reaction-distance figure at 55 mph, not perception distance.
explanations.b: The manual lists average perception time at 1.75 seconds, equating to about 142 feet at 55 mph.
explanations.c: 216 feet is the braking-distance figure at 55 mph on dry pavement with good brakes.
explanations.d: 419 feet is the total stopping distance at 55 mph, not the perception component alone.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: Combining perception, reaction, and braking distance, what does the CDL manual cite as the minimum total stopping distance for a heavy vehicle traveling 55 mph on dry pavement with good brakes?

answers.text: About 142 feet
About 216 feet
About 300 feet
About 419 feet, more than the length of a football field

explanations.a: 142 feet is just the perception-distance component at 55 mph.
explanations.b: 216 feet is just the braking-distance component at 55 mph.
explanations.c: The manual lists specific component figures that add to a larger number than 300 feet.
explanations.d: Adding the manual's components — about 142 feet perception, 61 feet reaction, and 216 feet braking — gives a minimum total of about 419 feet at 55 mph.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver doubles speed from 20 mph to 40 mph. According to the CDL manual's discussion of speed and stopping distance, by approximately what factor does braking distance increase?

answers.text: It doubles, increasing by about 2 times
It triples, increasing by about 3 times
It increases by about 4 times
It increases by about 16 times

explanations.a: Doubling speed does not simply double braking distance; energy increases with the square of speed.
explanations.b: Tripling is associated with going from 20 to 60 mph, which gives a 9x increase, not 3x.
explanations.c: The manual states that doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph increases impact and braking distance by about 4 times.
explanations.d: A 16-times increase is associated with going from 20 mph to 80 mph, not from 20 to 40 mph.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: Two identical tractor-trailers are tested on the same dry road. One is empty; the other is fully loaded within legal limits. According to the CDL manual, what does this comparison reveal about stopping distance?

answers.text: The empty truck always stops in a much shorter distance because it weighs less
The empty truck typically requires a greater stopping distance because it has less traction
Loaded and empty trucks stop in identical distances if brakes and tires are good
Empty trucks cannot legally be tested for stopping distance under FMCSA rules

explanations.a: While lighter weight reduces the work brakes must do, the loss of traction in an empty truck offsets that and can lengthen stopping distance.
explanations.b: The manual notes that brakes, tires, springs, and shock absorbers on heavy vehicles are designed to work best when fully loaded, so an empty truck has less traction and typically requires a longer stopping distance.
explanations.c: Loaded and empty stopping distances are not identical; load significantly affects traction and brake performance.
explanations.d: There is no FMCSA prohibition on stopping-distance testing for empty trucks.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: Of all the space around a heavy vehicle, the CDL manual identifies one specific area as the most important to manage. Which area is it?

answers.text: The space to the rear of the vehicle
The space ahead of the vehicle, into which it is driving
The space directly to the left of the driver
The space below the chassis at railroad crossings

explanations.a: Rear space matters but cannot be fully controlled; the manual specifies the area ahead is most important.
explanations.b: The manual states the space ahead — the space the vehicle is driving into — is the most important because the vehicle that trucks most often hit is the one in front of them, usually due to following too closely.
explanations.c: Side space matters for lane discipline, but it is not designated as the most important.
explanations.d: Space below is a concern at certain crossings and depressions, but it is not the most important overall.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: You realize a passenger car has been tailgating your tractor-trailer for several miles on a busy interstate. The CDL manual gives several recommended responses. Which is among them?

answers.text: Speed up to put more distance between you and the tailgater
Tap the brake lights repeatedly to warn the tailgater off
Increase your following distance ahead so you do not have to brake suddenly
Move into the left lane and slow to force the tailgater to go around

explanations.a: The manual specifically warns against speeding up because being tailgated at higher speed is more dangerous.
explanations.b: The manual cautions against flashing brake lights or other tricks because they can confuse or anger the tailgating driver.
explanations.c: The manual instructs drivers to increase their own following distance so they do not have to brake suddenly, giving the tailgater more room to get around.
explanations.d: Slowing aggressively in the left lane to punish a tailgater is consistent with aggressive driving, which the manual prohibits.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver of a 13'6" tall box trailer plans a route that includes a bridge posted at 13'8". The driver was empty under this bridge last week without incident, but is now loaded. What does the CDL manual say about trusting that posted clearance?

answers.text: Posted clearances are always accurate to within an inch and can be trusted
An empty trailer is shorter than a loaded one, so the past clearance proves the current trip is safe
Posted clearances apply only to school buses and passenger vehicles
Do not assume posted heights are correct; repaving or packed snow may have reduced the actual clearance

explanations.a: The manual specifically warns drivers not to assume posted heights are correct.
explanations.b: The manual states the opposite: an empty van is higher than a loaded one because the suspension extends.
explanations.c: Posted clearances apply to all vehicles; there is no carve-out by vehicle type.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers not to assume posted clearances are correct because repaving or packed snow may have reduced the actual clearance below the posted figure.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A tractor-trailer driver approaches a tight right turn at an intersection where the trailer cannot make the corner without swinging into the next lane. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct technique to complete the turn safely?

answers.text: Turn wide as you complete the turn while keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb
Swing wide to the left first to give the trailer plenty of room
Stop and back up if any vehicle is in the next lane, then complete the turn
Cross into oncoming traffic to give the trailer maximum clearance

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to turn wide as they complete the turn while keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb, which prevents other drivers from passing on the right.
explanations.b: Swinging wide to the left first invites following drivers to mistake the move for a left turn and pass on the right, causing crashes.
explanations.c: Backing up at an intersection is hazardous and can result in striking a vehicle that has stopped behind the truck.
explanations.d: Crossing into oncoming traffic without yielding is dangerous and not the manual's recommended method.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: Driving alongside another vehicle for an extended period creates two specific dangers identified in the CDL manual. Which pair of dangers does the manual list?

answers.text: Increased fuel consumption and tire wear
Another driver may change lanes into you, and you may be trapped when you need to change lanes
Reduced air-brake pressure and increased turbo lag
Trailer drift on uneven pavement and steering oscillation

explanations.a: Fuel and tire wear are not the safety hazards the manual identifies for side-by-side driving.
explanations.b: The CDL manual lists two specific dangers when traveling alongside other vehicles: another driver may change lanes suddenly into you, and you may be trapped when you need to change lanes yourself.
explanations.c: Brake pressure and turbo lag are mechanical concerns unrelated to side-space management.
explanations.d: Trailer drift and steering oscillation are not the side-space hazards the manual highlights.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual draws a careful distinction between a hazard and an emergency. Which definition matches the manual's use of the term hazard?

answers.text: A confirmed crash that has already occurred and is blocking the roadway
Any road condition or other road user that is a possible danger
A traffic citation issued during a roadside inspection
A weather warning broadcast by the National Weather Service

explanations.a: A crash that has already happened is a different category of incident; the manual defines hazard as a possibility of danger, not a realized event.
explanations.b: The manual defines a hazard as any road condition or other road user that is a possible danger, distinct from an emergency in which the danger is now immediate.
explanations.c: Traffic citations are administrative, not the manual's definition of hazard.
explanations.d: Weather warnings may indicate hazardous conditions but are not the manual's definition of the term itself.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual emphasizes that recognizing hazards early gives a driver something specific. What does the manual identify as the main benefit of seeing hazards before they become emergencies?

answers.text: It guarantees the hazard will not develop into an emergency
It allows the driver to ignore the hazard and keep moving normally
It gives the driver more time to plan a response before the hazard becomes an emergency
It exempts the driver from liability if a crash subsequently occurs

explanations.a: Early recognition does not prevent hazards from escalating; it provides time to react.
explanations.b: Ignoring a recognized hazard contradicts the manual's instruction to plan a response.
explanations.c: The manual states that early recognition of hazards gives a driver more time to plan a response before the hazard escalates into an emergency.
explanations.d: Liability outcomes are legal matters, not the safety benefit the manual identifies.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: While driving on a multi-lane road, you notice a moving van with the rear window completely blocked by cargo. The CDL manual classifies certain other drivers as predictable hazards. Why does it identify a driver with blocked vision as one of these hazards?

answers.text: Such drivers are exempt from federal motor-carrier rules
They are required by law to drive faster than other vehicles
Their vehicles cannot legally use the right lane on highways
Drivers who cannot see other vehicles are likely to make moves without seeing the CMV beside or behind them

explanations.a: Exemption from motor-carrier rules has nothing to do with hazard recognition.
explanations.b: There is no rule requiring blocked-vision drivers to travel at higher speeds.
explanations.c: There is no lane restriction tied to a driver's vision being blocked.
explanations.d: The manual identifies blocked-vision drivers as hazards because they cannot see other vehicles and may merge, brake, or turn without seeing the CMV around them.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A red triangle with an orange center mounted on the rear of a vehicle is a federally recognized warning emblem. According to the CDL manual, what does this emblem identify?

answers.text: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials
A school bus stopping for a railroad crossing
A slow-moving vehicle, often farm or construction equipment
An out-of-service CMV awaiting roadside repair

explanations.a: Hazardous materials are identified by diamond-shaped placards, not the slow-moving-vehicle emblem.
explanations.b: School buses are identified by their distinctive paint, lights, and signage, not this triangle.
explanations.c: The manual specifies that a red triangle with an orange center is the slow-moving-vehicle symbol, often seen on farm or construction equipment.
explanations.d: Out-of-service vehicles use OOS stickers and roadside warning devices, not the slow-moving-vehicle emblem.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.7 Distracted driving, aggressive driving, road rage
questions.text: Federal research cited in the CDL manual gives a striking figure for the increased odds of a safety-critical event when CMV drivers text behind the wheel. Approximately how much greater are those odds compared to drivers who do not text?

answers.text: About 23 times greater
About 2 times greater
About 6 times greater
About 50 times greater

explanations.a: The manual cites research showing the odds of a safety-critical event are about 23.2 times greater for CMV drivers who text while driving compared to those who do not.
explanations.b: Doubling the odds understates the actual increase reported in the manual.
explanations.c: Six times greater is the figure the manual associates with dialing a mobile phone, not texting.
explanations.d: Fifty times is higher than the manual's published figure for texting.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.7 Distracted driving, aggressive driving, road rage
questions.text: Federal regulations restrict how a CMV driver may use a mobile phone. Which restriction matches the rule discussed in the CDL manual?

answers.text: Drivers may dial freely as long as the phone is not held to the ear
Drivers may text any time the vehicle is moving below 25 mph
Drivers may hold and read a paper map while driving but not a mobile phone
Drivers may not hold a mobile phone for a voice call or dial it by pressing more than a single button while driving

explanations.a: Even hands-free dialing is restricted; drivers may not press more than a single button on the device while driving.
explanations.b: There is no speed-based exception that allows texting at low speeds.
explanations.c: The manual addresses mobile-phone use specifically; it does not authorize handling other distractions.
explanations.d: Federal rules prohibit holding a mobile phone for a voice call or dialing it by pressing more than a single button while driving a CMV.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.7 Distracted driving, aggressive driving, road rage
questions.text: The CDL manual draws a clear distinction between aggressive driving and road rage. Which pair of definitions matches the manual's wording?

answers.text: Aggressive driving is a felony; road rage is a civil infraction
Aggressive driving is operating selfishly, boldly, or pushily; road rage is operating with the intent to harm another driver
Aggressive driving is following too closely only; road rage is speeding only
Aggressive driving is permitted in commercial vehicles; road rage is permitted only in passenger cars

explanations.a: The manual does not classify these by criminal-law tier; it defines them by behavior.
explanations.b: The manual defines aggressive driving as operating in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner without regard for others, and road rage as operating with the intent to do harm to another driver.
explanations.c: Both terms are broader than a single behavior such as following too closely or speeding.
explanations.d: Neither aggressive driving nor road rage is permitted in any vehicle type.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.7 Distracted driving, aggressive driving, road rage
questions.text: The CDL manual cites a striking statistic on the effect of even a small distraction on crash rates. According to the manual, if drivers react half a second slower because of distractions, what happens to crash rates?

answers.text: Crashes are reduced by half
Crashes increase by 10 percent
Crashes double
There is no measurable change in crash rates

explanations.a: A distraction-induced delay does not reduce crashes; it increases them.
explanations.b: A 10-percent increase understates the manual's published figure.
explanations.c: The manual states that if drivers react half a second slower because of distractions, crashes double.
explanations.d: The manual reports a measurable increase, not a null effect.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual gives an approximate forward illumination range for low-beam headlights at night. About how far ahead do low beams illuminate the road?

answers.text: About 100 feet
About 500 feet
About 250 feet
About 1,000 feet

explanations.a: 100 feet underestimates the manual's stated low-beam range.
explanations.b: 500 feet overstates low-beam range and approaches the high-end figure for high beams.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states drivers can see ahead about 250 feet with low beams.
explanations.d: 1,000 feet is well beyond the headlight range listed in the manual.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: At night with high beams on and clean lenses, the CDL manual gives an approximate range that headlights illuminate ahead. About how far is that range?

answers.text: Roughly 125 feet
Roughly 800 feet
Roughly 200 feet, slightly below the low-beam figure
About 350 to 500 feet

explanations.a: 125 feet is well below the manual's stated high-beam range.
explanations.b: 800 feet far exceeds the figure given in the manual.
explanations.c: 200 feet is below both the low-beam and high-beam figures cited in the manual.
explanations.d: The manual states drivers can see about 350 to 500 feet with high beams.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: At night, the CDL manual recommends adjusting speed so the vehicle can stop within a specific distance. Which distance limit matches the manual's rule for night driving?

answers.text: Within twice the distance the headlights illuminate
Within the distance illuminated by the headlights
Within the distance the wipers can clear in five seconds
Within whichever speed limit is posted, regardless of headlight range

explanations.a: Twice the headlight range is unsafe because the driver could not stop within actual sight distance.
explanations.b: The manual instructs drivers to adjust speed so the stopping distance stays within the range illuminated by the headlights.
explanations.c: Wiper performance is a wet-weather concern, not the night-driving sight-distance rule.
explanations.d: Posted limits set the maximum, but the manual requires drivers to slow further when sight distance is shorter than stopping distance.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: You are driving at night on a two-lane rural highway with your high beams on, and an oncoming vehicle approaches. The CDL manual provides guidance for high-beam use during oncoming traffic. What is the proper action?

answers.text: Switch to low beams in time to avoid blinding the oncoming driver, well before passing
Keep high beams on until the oncoming vehicle's headlights pass the rear of your trailer
Flash high beams repeatedly to make sure the other driver sees you
Turn the headlights off entirely while the other vehicle is alongside

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to dim high beams in time to avoid blinding oncoming drivers.
explanations.b: Keeping high beams on through the pass blinds the oncoming driver and creates a head-on risk.
explanations.c: Flashing high beams creates more glare and can be mistaken as an aggressive signal.
explanations.d: Turning off headlights leaves the truck invisible and is never appropriate at night.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.9 Driving in fog, rain, snow, ice
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a single piece of best advice for driving in dense fog. Which statement matches the manual's recommendation?

answers.text: Maintain normal speed and trust your headlights to cut through the fog
Use high beams to maximize visibility through the fog
Tailgate a leading vehicle to use its taillights as a guide
The best advice is don't; pull off the road into a rest area until the fog lifts

explanations.a: Maintaining normal speed in fog is the opposite of the manual's advice.
explanations.b: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; the manual does not recommend them.
explanations.c: Tailgating is unsafe at any time and especially dangerous when visibility is reduced.
explanations.d: The manual states that the best advice for driving in fog is don't; if possible, pull off the road into a rest area until the fog lifts.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.9 Driving in fog, rain, snow, ice
questions.text: On a wet road, the CDL manual gives a specific guideline for reducing speed compared to dry-pavement operation. By approximately how much should a driver reduce speed on a wet road?

answers.text: By about 10 percent
By about half
By about one-third, for example slowing from 55 to about 35 mph
To a crawl, regardless of visibility

explanations.a: A 10-percent reduction is too small for the traction loss the manual describes on wet pavement.
explanations.b: Half-speed reduction is the manual's guideline for packed snow, not wet pavement.
explanations.c: The manual instructs drivers to reduce speed by about one-third on a wet road, for example slowing from 55 to about 35 mph.
explanations.d: Crawling is reserved for icy surfaces, not wet pavement.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.9 Driving in fog, rain, snow, ice
questions.text: You sense your tractor-trailer hydroplaning at about 50 mph during heavy rain. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct response to regain control?

answers.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow the vehicle and let the wheels turn freely
Apply the brakes firmly to stop as quickly as possible
Steer aggressively in the opposite direction of the lane to break the water film
Speed up to lift the front of the trailer above the water

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to release the accelerator and push in the clutch when hydroplaning, slowing the vehicle and allowing the wheels to turn freely so they can regain road contact.
explanations.b: The manual specifically warns that braking during hydroplaning can worsen loss of control.
explanations.c: Sharp steering inputs during hydroplaning can cause the vehicle to skid as soon as traction returns.
explanations.d: Increasing speed makes hydroplaning more severe, not less.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.9 Driving in fog, rain, snow, ice
questions.text: Black ice is one of the most dangerous winter hazards. According to the CDL manual, what visual clue suggests the road may be coated in black ice?

answers.text: The road appears white and chalky in patches
The road looks wet when the temperature is at or below freezing
The road has a yellow tint under the headlights
The road shows visible cracks running parallel to the lane

explanations.a: White, chalky patches suggest packed snow or salt residue, not black ice.
explanations.b: The manual describes black ice as a thin, clear layer that makes the road look wet; whenever the temperature is at or below freezing and the road looks wet, drivers should suspect black ice.
explanations.c: A yellow tint is not the manual's described visual cue for black ice.
explanations.d: Pavement cracks indicate road condition, not ice.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.9 Driving in fog, rain, snow, ice
questions.text: In near-freezing weather, the CDL manual identifies one specific roadway feature that becomes icy before the rest of the road. Which feature is it, and at roughly what temperature should drivers be most alert?

answers.text: Tunnels, especially below 50°F
Asphalt patches, especially above 40°F
Bridges and overpasses, especially when the temperature is close to 32°F
Concrete shoulders, especially above 45°F

explanations.a: Tunnels are sheltered and tend to stay slightly warmer than the open road.
explanations.b: Asphalt patches do not freeze before bridges; the manual specifically calls out bridges.
explanations.c: The manual states that bridges and overpasses freeze before the rest of the road and warns drivers to be especially careful when the temperature is close to 32°F.
explanations.d: Concrete shoulders are not the manual's identified early-freezing surface.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.10 Mountain driving and runaway escape ramps
questions.text: On a long, steep downgrade, the CDL manual identifies a principal way to control vehicle speed without overheating the brakes. Which is it?

answers.text: Riding the service brake firmly to keep speed at exactly the safe target
Using the braking effect of the engine as the principal way to control speed
Putting the transmission in neutral to coast
Activating only the trailer brakes and saving the tractor brakes

explanations.a: Riding the service brake heats them up and leads to brake fade, which the manual specifically warns against.
explanations.b: The manual states that drivers must use the braking effect of the engine as the principal way of controlling speed on downgrades.
explanations.c: Coasting in neutral removes engine braking entirely and is unsafe on downgrades.
explanations.d: Using only trailer brakes overheats them and can cause loss of control.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.10 Mountain driving and runaway escape ramps
questions.text: Before beginning a long, steep descent, the CDL manual specifies the correct moment to select the appropriate gear. When should the driver shift to the proper low gear?

answers.text: Before starting down the grade, while the vehicle is still on level pavement at the top
Halfway down the grade, after assessing actual speed buildup
Only after the brakes have begun to fade
At the bottom of the grade, after the steepest portion has been completed

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to shift to a low gear before starting down the grade, because once speed builds up the driver may not be able to downshift at all.
explanations.b: Waiting until the middle of the grade may make it impossible to downshift, leaving the driver without engine braking.
explanations.c: Brake fade is a failure mode the manual seeks to prevent through proper pre-grade gear selection, not a trigger for shifting.
explanations.d: Shifting at the bottom of the grade is far too late to influence the descent.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.10 Mountain driving and runaway escape ramps
questions.text: The CDL manual describes a specific snub-braking technique for long downgrades. According to the manual, the driver should apply the brakes hard enough to feel a definite slowdown, then release them when speed has dropped by approximately how much below the chosen safe speed?

answers.text: About 15 mph below the safe speed
Exactly half the safe speed
About 5 mph below the safe speed
Whenever the brakes start to smoke

explanations.a: A 15-mph reduction is more than the manual's stated technique and would extend brake-application time.
explanations.b: Cutting speed in half is far more aggressive than the technique described in the manual.
explanations.c: The manual instructs drivers to apply the brakes until speed has been reduced about 5 mph below their chosen safe speed, then release them, with the application lasting roughly three seconds.
explanations.d: Smoke indicates failure, not the trigger to release brakes; the technique uses speed targets, not visible smoke.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.10 Mountain driving and runaway escape ramps
questions.text: You are descending a steep grade and your service brakes have lost effectiveness. An escape ramp is posted ahead. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct decision?

answers.text: Avoid the ramp because using it always damages the cargo and the vehicle beyond repair
Pass the ramp and try to limp the vehicle to the next exit, hoping brakes recover
Wait until the brakes are completely gone before considering the ramp
Use the escape ramp; the manual states that not using an available ramp greatly increases the chance of a serious crash

explanations.a: Some cargo and equipment damage may occur, but the manual emphasizes ramp use saves lives.
explanations.b: Passing the ramp gives speed and gravity more time to build, making any subsequent recovery harder.
explanations.c: Waiting until brakes are completely gone may put the ramp out of reach.
explanations.d: The manual instructs drivers to use an available escape ramp because escape ramps are designed to stop runaway vehicles safely; not using one greatly increases the chance of a serious crash.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a typical clearance time for a tractor-trailer to traverse a single railroad track. About how many seconds does the manual say it takes for a typical tractor-trailer to clear a single track?

answers.text: At least 5 seconds
At least 14 seconds
At least 30 seconds
At least 60 seconds

explanations.a: Five seconds is far less than the time the manual gives for a typical tractor-trailer.
explanations.b: The manual states it takes a typical tractor-trailer at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.
explanations.c: Thirty seconds is well above the manual's typical clearance time for a single track.
explanations.d: Sixty seconds is far above the manual's stated clearance time and is closer to a stalled-vehicle figure.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: While crossing a railroad track in a manual-transmission tractor-trailer, the CDL manual gives a specific instruction about shifting. Which of the following matches the manual's rule?

answers.text: Do not shift gears while crossing the tracks
Always downshift to first gear once both axles are on the tracks
Shift to neutral and coast across the tracks
Apply the trailer hand valve while crossing to keep the trailer back

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers not to shift gears while crossing railroad tracks because a missed shift could leave the rig stalled on the rails.
explanations.b: Downshifting while on the tracks creates the exact missed-shift risk the manual warns against.
explanations.c: Coasting in neutral removes drive power and can leave the vehicle stranded if torque is suddenly needed.
explanations.d: Using the trailer hand valve to slow only the trailer while crossing tracks risks losing all forward momentum.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver's tractor-trailer becomes stuck on a railroad-highway grade crossing. The CDL manual gives a specific safety procedure for this situation. Which step does it instruct first?

answers.text: Stay in the cab and try to rock the vehicle off the tracks using the throttle
Walk the tracks in both directions and signal any approaching train
Wait for a passing motorist to call the railroad emergency line
Get out of the vehicle and away from the tracks, then call the emergency number posted at the crossing or 911

explanations.a: Staying in the cab leaves the driver in the most dangerous spot if a train arrives.
explanations.b: Walking the tracks puts the driver in the path of any approaching train.
explanations.c: Waiting for a passerby is too slow; the manual prescribes immediate driver action.
explanations.d: The manual instructs drivers to get out of the vehicle and away from the tracks, then call 911 or the emergency number posted at the crossing, providing the DOT crossing number if visible.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver approaches a passive grade crossing with a clear view down the tracks and sees a train approaching at some distance. The CDL manual gives a clear instruction about racing trains to crossings. Which statement reflects the manual's rule and the underlying reason?

answers.text: Race the train if the driver judges the truck to be faster than the train
Cross only if the train horn has not yet sounded a long blast
Never race a train to a crossing because the speed of an approaching train is extremely difficult to judge
Cross only if the lead engine appears to be at least the length of three football fields away

explanations.a: The manual specifically warns drivers never to race a train to a crossing.
explanations.b: Trains may not sound horns at every public crossing, so the absence of a horn is not a safe gauge of train distance.
explanations.c: The manual instructs drivers never to race a train to a crossing because it is extremely difficult to judge the speed of an approaching train.
explanations.d: The manual does not provide a football-field rule for crossing, and visual estimation of train distance is not reliable.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.12 Driving emergencies (steering, braking, escape paths, blowouts)
questions.text: In an emergency where the driver does not have enough room to stop, the CDL manual gives a key principle for choosing between steering away and trying to stop. What does the manual say?

answers.text: Always try to stop, since steering at high speed will cause a rollover
You can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
Always lock the brakes to stop in the shortest possible distance
Always swerve into oncoming traffic because that lane will usually be clear

explanations.a: Steering away is often faster than stopping; the manual specifically points this out.
explanations.b: The manual states that you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop, so steering is often the right emergency action.
explanations.c: Locking the brakes causes skidding and loss of steering control, which the manual specifically warns against.
explanations.d: Swerving into oncoming traffic creates a head-on collision risk and is the opposite of the manual's guidance.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.12 Driving emergencies (steering, braking, escape paths, blowouts)
questions.text: A loud bang and a sudden 'heavy' steering feel suggest a front tire has blown on a tractor-trailer at highway speed. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct immediate response?

answers.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands and stay off the brake until the vehicle slows down
Apply the service brakes hard and steer toward the shoulder immediately
Pull the parking-brake valve to stop the vehicle quickly
Release the steering wheel briefly to let the vehicle find its own line

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to hold the wheel firmly with both hands and stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed; braking immediately after a tire failure can cause loss of control.
explanations.b: Hard braking after a tire failure can cause skidding, jackknife, or rollover.
explanations.c: Yanking the parking-brake valve at highway speed will lock the wheels and almost certainly cause loss of control.
explanations.d: Releasing the wheel during a blowout virtually guarantees loss of control because the failed tire pulls the vehicle.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.12 Driving emergencies (steering, braking, escape paths, blowouts)
questions.text: The CDL manual describes counter-steering as part of an emergency steering action. Which description matches the manual's discussion?

answers.text: Counter-steering means braking hard while turning to keep the vehicle level
Counter-steering means steering only with the left hand to maintain mirror contact
Counter-steering means leaving the steering wheel centered and letting the vehicle correct itself
Counter-steering means turning the wheel back the other direction once you have passed whatever was in your path

explanations.a: Braking while turning is exactly what the manual warns against during emergency maneuvers.
explanations.b: Single-hand steering during a counter-steer is unsafe; the manual emphasizes both hands.
explanations.c: Letting the wheel center itself does not counter-steer; the manual describes an active second steering input.
explanations.d: The manual describes counter-steering as turning the wheel back in the other direction once the obstacle has been passed, treating emergency steering and counter-steering as two parts of one action.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.12 Driving emergencies (steering, braking, escape paths, blowouts)
questions.text: A driver is forced off the right edge of a highway onto the shoulder during a sudden emergency. According to the CDL manual, what is the recommended way to handle braking and tire placement on the shoulder?

answers.text: Brake immediately at full pressure to slow the vehicle as fast as possible
Get all four wheels onto the shoulder to maximize traction
Avoid using the brakes until speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake gently, and keep one set of wheels on the pavement if possible
Apply the parking brake to stop the vehicle in the shortest distance

explanations.a: Hard braking on a loose shoulder surface will cause skidding and loss of control.
explanations.b: Pulling all four wheels off the pavement reduces overall control; the manual recommends keeping one set on the pavement.
explanations.c: The manual instructs drivers to avoid using the brakes until speed drops to about 20 mph, then brake gently, and keep at least one set of wheels on the pavement to maintain control.
explanations.d: Yanking the parking brake at speed locks the wheels and risks loss of control.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.12 Driving emergencies (steering, braking, escape paths, blowouts)
questions.text: A driver of a hydraulically braked CMV experiences a brake-pedal feel that has gone soft and is sinking toward the floor on a level road. The CDL manual gives several specific recovery steps. Which of the following is among them?

answers.text: Pump the brake pedal because pumping can sometimes restore hydraulic pressure long enough to stop
Hold the pedal flat to the floor until pressure returns
Shut off the engine immediately so the brakes can self-bleed
Steer onto the shoulder at full speed and use no other actions

explanations.a: The manual lists pumping the brake pedal as a step that can sometimes generate enough hydraulic pressure to slow the vehicle, alongside downshifting and using the parking brake gradually.
explanations.b: Holding the pedal flat does nothing to restore hydraulic pressure.
explanations.c: Shutting off the engine eliminates power steering and power-assist braking and does not bleed the system.
explanations.d: Doing nothing else but steering ignores the manual's clear list of pumping, downshifting, parking-brake use, and seeking an escape route.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual makes one important point clear about what antilock braking systems do and do not do for a CMV. Which statement matches the manual's wording?

answers.text: ABS guarantees a shorter stopping distance under all conditions
ABS replaces the conventional brake system entirely
ABS allows drivers to follow more closely than they otherwise would
ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, but it helps the driver keep the vehicle under control during hard braking

explanations.a: The manual specifically denies that ABS shortens stopping distance.
explanations.b: ABS is an addition to the normal brakes, not a replacement; the manual is explicit on that point.
explanations.c: The manual states ABS does not allow drivers to follow more closely or drive less carefully.
explanations.d: The manual states ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, but it helps the driver keep the vehicle under control during hard braking by preventing wheel lockup.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: On a trailer equipped with antilock brakes, the manufacturer must mount a malfunction indicator lamp at a specific location. Where does the CDL manual say drivers should look for the trailer ABS malfunction lamp?

answers.text: On the right rear corner of the trailer
On the front bumper of the tractor
On the left side of the trailer, at the front or rear corner
On the dashboard of the tractor only, never on the trailer itself

explanations.a: The manual specifies the left side of the trailer, not the right rear corner.
explanations.b: Tractor ABS lamps are on the dashboard, but the trailer ABS lamp is on the trailer.
explanations.c: The manual states trailer ABS malfunction lamps are on the left side of the trailer, either on the front or rear corner.
explanations.d: Tractor and trailer have separate ABS lamps; the trailer lamp is on the trailer body, not only the dash.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The Department of Transportation set specific phase-in dates for required antilock braking systems on different vehicle types. According to the CDL manual, when did ABS become required on truck tractors with air brakes?

answers.text: Built on or after March 1, 1995
Built on or after March 1, 1997
Built on or after March 1, 1999
Built on or after March 1, 2001

explanations.a: March 1, 1995 is not a date the manual lists for ABS phase-in.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
explanations.c: March 1, 1999 is the date for hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or more, not air-braked tractors.
explanations.d: March 1, 2001 is not one of the manual's listed ABS phase-in dates.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver of a straight truck with working ABS on all axles encounters a sudden emergency that requires maximum braking. According to the CDL manual, what braking technique is permitted in this specific case?

answers.text: Fully apply the brakes, because working ABS on all axles will manage wheel lockup
Pump the brakes rapidly to keep the wheels from locking
Apply only the parking brake to avoid overheating the service brakes
Brake gently to prevent the ABS from activating, since activation damages the system

explanations.a: The manual provides one exception to normal brake-pedal modulation: in a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, in an emergency stop, the driver may fully apply the brakes.
explanations.b: Pumping the brakes is associated with non-ABS hydraulic-failure recovery; with working ABS, the system manages lockup automatically.
explanations.c: Yanking the parking brake at speed locks the wheels and is the wrong response.
explanations.d: ABS activation does not damage the system; activation is the system functioning as designed.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual identifies a small set of root causes for nearly all serious skids. Which group of four matches the manual's list?

answers.text: Cold tires, hot brakes, low fuel, high winds
Wet pavement, dry pavement, cobblestones, gravel
Heavy load, light load, bobtail, deadhead
Over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast

explanations.a: These factors can contribute to traction problems but are not the manual's four named causes of skids.
explanations.b: Surface types can reduce traction but are not the manual's named causes of skids.
explanations.c: Load conditions affect traction but are not the four named skid causes.
explanations.d: The manual identifies four causes of skids: over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast for conditions.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver feels the rear drive wheels of a tractor-trailer break loose in a braking skid on a slick road. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct first action to recover?

answers.text: Stop braking to let the rear wheels roll again and regain traction
Apply more brake pressure to lock the wheels evenly
Pull the trailer hand valve to slow only the trailer
Steer hard in the direction the rear is sliding, then keep that input until the rig straightens

explanations.a: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again and regain traction.
explanations.b: Adding brake pressure deepens the lock-up and worsens the skid.
explanations.c: The trailer hand valve slows only the trailer and can worsen a drive-wheel skid; the manual does not recommend it for this situation.
explanations.d: Holding a single-direction steering input ignores the counter-steer step and can cause a skid in the opposite direction.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: During a front-wheel skid, the CDL manual describes a specific way the vehicle behaves. Which description matches the manual's account of front-wheel skid?

answers.text: The vehicle spins quickly toward the side of the skid until it comes to rest
The vehicle's rear wheels rise off the road and push the front into the curb
The vehicle accelerates uncontrollably regardless of throttle position
The front end tends to go in a straight line regardless of how much you turn the steering wheel

explanations.a: That behavior describes a rear-wheel spin-out, not a front-wheel skid.
explanations.b: Rear wheels rising and pushing the front is not the manual's description of a front-wheel skid.
explanations.c: Front-wheel skid does not cause uncontrolled acceleration.
explanations.d: The manual states that in a front-wheel skid, the front end tends to go in a straight line regardless of steering input.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual warns that after counter-steering out of a drive-wheel skid, drivers must be ready for a specific follow-up reaction. What does the manual specifically warn drivers to be prepared for?

answers.text: Sudden tire deflation due to lateral force on the sidewalls
The vehicle's tendency to keep on turning, which means you may have to steer back the other way to avoid skidding the opposite direction
Loss of all engine power for several seconds after the skid
Automatic lockout of the steering column for diagnostic purposes

explanations.a: Sidewall failure is not the manual's warned-against follow-up reaction.
explanations.b: The manual specifically warns that after the vehicle turns back on course it has a tendency to keep on turning, so the driver may have to steer the wheel back the other way to avoid skidding in the opposite direction.
explanations.c: There is no engine-power loss tied to skid recovery in the manual.
explanations.d: Steering columns do not lock during skid recovery.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.15 Accident procedures (protect scene, notify, help injured)
questions.text: At any accident scene, the CDL manual lists three basic steps in order. Which set of three steps matches the manual's order?

answers.text: Protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured
Photograph damage, exchange insurance, drive to the next exit
Move all vehicles, call dispatch, request a tow truck
File a written report, contact the insurer, request a replacement vehicle

explanations.a: The CDL manual lists the three basic accident-scene steps as protecting the area, notifying authorities, and caring for the injured.
explanations.b: These are post-incident administrative steps, not the manual's three immediate actions.
explanations.c: The manual does not instruct drivers to move all vehicles or call dispatch as the three core steps.
explanations.d: Reporting and insurance steps come later; the manual's first three steps are different.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.15 Accident procedures (protect scene, notify, help injured)
questions.text: To prevent a secondary crash at an accident scene, the CDL manual instructs drivers to use specific warning equipment as part of protecting the area. Which of the following is part of that protection step?

answers.text: Spread cargo netting across the lane to slow approaching traffic
Set out reflective triangles so other drivers can see them in time to avoid the accident
Wave a personal flashlight in the lane while standing in the traffic flow
Pour engine oil on the road to make a visible warning slick

explanations.a: The manual does not instruct drivers to spread cargo netting; it instructs drivers to use reflective triangles and four-way flashers.
explanations.b: The manual specifies setting out reflective triangles so other drivers can see them in time to avoid the accident, alongside turning on four-way flashers.
explanations.c: Standing in the traffic flow with a flashlight is hazardous and is not the manual's protection method.
explanations.d: Pouring oil creates a new hazard and is the opposite of protecting the scene.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.15 Accident procedures (protect scene, notify, help injured)
questions.text: At a crash scene with a severely injured occupant pinned inside a damaged vehicle, the CDL manual gives specific guidance about whether to move that person. Which option matches the manual's instruction?

answers.text: Move every injured person out of the vehicle as quickly as possible to make medical care easier
Lift the injured person clear and lay them on the pavement to assess injuries
Do not move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
Always move the injured person at least 100 feet from any vehicle for safety

explanations.a: Moving a severely injured person can worsen spinal or internal injuries; this is the opposite of the manual's instruction.
explanations.b: Lifting an injured person without medical training can worsen injuries and is not the manual's recommended approach.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers not to move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
explanations.d: There is no 100-foot rule for moving injured persons in the manual.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.15 Accident procedures (protect scene, notify, help injured)
questions.text: At a crash scene where an injured occupant is bleeding heavily and no emergency responders have yet arrived, the CDL manual provides simple first-aid guidance. Which step does the manual recommend?

answers.text: Apply a tourniquet at full strength on the chest regardless of wound location
Pour water onto the wound to wash away contaminants until paramedics arrive
Place the injured person in a seated position regardless of injury type
Apply direct pressure to the wound to stop heavy bleeding, and keep the injured person warm

explanations.a: A chest tourniquet is not appropriate first aid and is not in the manual.
explanations.b: Pouring water is not the manual's instruction for severe bleeding.
explanations.c: Placing the injured person in a seated position regardless of injury can worsen spinal or chest injuries.
explanations.d: The manual instructs drivers to stop heavy bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound and to keep the injured person warm.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: During an electrical fire in a CMV, the CDL manual specifies a single specific type of extinguishing approach. Which approach is correct for an electrical fire?

answers.text: Use water as the primary agent because it cools fastest
Use a non-conducting agent such as carbon dioxide or dry chemicals; do not use water
Use foam first, then chase with water
Use sand mixed with diesel fuel to smother the fire

explanations.a: The manual specifically warns drivers not to use water on an electrical fire because water can conduct electricity and cause shock.
explanations.b: The manual instructs drivers to extinguish electrical fires (Class C) with non-conducting agents such as carbon dioxide or dry chemicals.
explanations.c: Foam followed by water is not the manual's prescribed method for electrical fires.
explanations.d: Mixing combustible diesel fuel into a fire scene is dangerous and not in the manual.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: The CDL manual describes two common types of extinguisher labels for CMVs. Which option correctly distinguishes a B:C extinguisher from an A:B:C extinguisher?

answers.text: B:C is for ammunition fires only; A:B:C is for liquid fires only
B:C is for tire fires; A:B:C is for engine fires
B:C is designed to work on electrical fires and burning liquids; A:B:C is also designed to work on burning wood, paper, and cloth
B:C is for hazmat only; A:B:C is for cargo fires only

explanations.a: Ammunition is in the explosives class, not the B:C designation; the labels do not refer to ammunition versus liquid only.
explanations.b: Tire-fire and engine-fire categorization is not how B:C and A:B:C are distinguished.
explanations.c: The manual states the B:C extinguisher is designed to work on electrical fires and burning liquids, while the A:B:C extinguisher is also designed to work on burning wood, paper, and cloth.
explanations.d: The labels apply to fire classes, not to cargo type.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: When operating a fire extinguisher on a vehicle fire, the CDL manual gives a specific aiming instruction. Where should the operator direct the discharge?

answers.text: At the source or base of the fire, not up in the flames
At the highest visible flame so the agent rains down
At the surrounding pavement to cool the area first
At the smoke column to break apart the rising plume

explanations.a: The manual instructs operators to aim at the source or base of the fire, not up in the flames.
explanations.b: Aiming at the highest flames wastes agent because it does not reach the fuel source.
explanations.c: Cooling the surrounding pavement does not extinguish the fire.
explanations.d: Smoke is a product of the fire, not its fuel source; aiming at smoke does not extinguish flames.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.text: A driver discovers a fire inside a closed cargo van trailer at a rest stop. The CDL manual gives a clear instruction about whether to open the trailer doors. Which option matches the manual's instruction and the underlying reason?

answers.text: Open the doors immediately to vent smoke and reduce pressure inside
Open one door at a time to inspect cargo and apply water through the gap
Open the doors only if the cargo is hazardous materials, to release toxic gas
Keep the doors shut, especially if the cargo contains hazardous materials, because opening them supplies oxygen and can make the fire burn very fast

explanations.a: Opening the doors floods the fire with oxygen and can cause a flashover.
explanations.b: Even partial opening introduces oxygen and is not the manual's recommended action.
explanations.c: The manual specifically says to keep the doors shut, especially with hazardous materials, not to vent toxic gas by opening them.
explanations.d: The manual instructs drivers to keep the doors shut on a cargo-van fire, especially if the cargo contains hazardous materials, because opening them supplies oxygen and can make the fire burn very fast.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.17 Alcohol, drugs, and other impairing substances
questions.text: The CDL manual explains that only time can reduce blood alcohol concentration because of how the body metabolizes alcohol. About how much alcohol can the liver process per hour, according to the manual?

answers.text: About a full ounce per hour
About one full standard drink every 15 minutes
About one full standard drink every 30 minutes
About one-third of an ounce of alcohol per hour, less than the alcohol in one standard drink

explanations.a: A full ounce per hour overstates the body's processing rate.
explanations.b: A standard drink every 15 minutes far exceeds liver processing.
explanations.c: A standard drink every 30 minutes still exceeds the rate the manual gives.
explanations.d: The manual states the liver can process only about one-third of an ounce of alcohol per hour, considerably less than the alcohol in a standard drink.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.17 Alcohol, drugs, and other impairing substances
questions.text: The CDL manual explains that several drink types contain the same amount of alcohol. Which set of three drinks does the manual identify as containing equal alcohol?

answers.text: A 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor
A 32-ounce mug of beer, an 8-ounce glass of wine, and a 4-ounce shot of vodka
A 16-ounce can of malt beverage, a 6-ounce glass of port, and a 2.5-ounce shot of whiskey
A 12-ounce glass of 12% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 5% wine, and a 1-ounce shot of 100-proof rum

explanations.a: The CDL manual identifies these three drinks — a 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor — as containing the same amount of alcohol.
explanations.b: These quantities are well above standard drink sizes and contain more alcohol than the manual's equivalence.
explanations.c: These sizes and proofs do not match the manual's equivalence.
explanations.d: These percentages are reversed and do not match the manual's stated equivalence.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.17 Alcohol, drugs, and other impairing substances
questions.text: A coworker offers a cup of black coffee to a driver who has consumed alcohol, claiming it will help him sober up before driving. According to the CDL manual, what does the manual say about coffee, cold showers, and other sobering tactics?

answers.text: Black coffee accelerates liver metabolism by about 50 percent
Only time, not black coffee or a cold shower, will sober a driver up
Cold showers reduce blood alcohol concentration by about 25 percent
Caffeine and cold water together fully reverse alcohol impairment within 30 minutes

explanations.a: The manual states the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate; coffee does not change that rate.
explanations.b: The manual states that only time, not black coffee or a cold shower, will sober a driver up because liver metabolism is at a fixed rate.
explanations.c: Cold showers do not lower blood alcohol concentration; the manual specifically denies this.
explanations.d: Caffeine and cold water do not reverse alcohol impairment.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.17 Alcohol, drugs, and other impairing substances
questions.text: A driver is prescribed an antihistamine that lists drowsiness as a side effect. According to the CDL manual's discussion of drugs and driving, what is the proper consideration before driving a CMV on this medication?

answers.text: Prescription drugs never cause impairment, so the driver may proceed normally
The driver may operate the CMV as long as the prescription label has the driver's name on it
The driver must follow doctor's orders and warning labels, and may operate a CMV only if the prescriber confirms it will not affect safe driving ability
Mixing the antihistamine with one alcoholic drink is allowed if at least four hours have passed

explanations.a: The manual recognizes that prescription drugs can impair driving and instructs drivers to follow warning labels.
explanations.b: The presence of the driver's name on the bottle does not address whether the medication impairs driving.
explanations.c: The manual instructs drivers to pay attention to warning labels for legitimate drugs and medicines and to doctor's orders, and to operate a CMV only when the prescriber confirms it will not affect safe driving ability.
explanations.d: The manual specifically warns that alcohol can make the effects of other drugs much worse and recommends not mixing drugs with driving at all.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.18 Staying alert and fit to drive
questions.text: To maintain alertness on long trips, the CDL manual gives a periodic-break recommendation. About how often does the manual suggest taking a break during long trips?

answers.text: Every 50 miles or 1 hour, whichever comes first
Every 250 miles or 5 hours, whichever comes first
About every 100 miles or 2 hours during long trips
Only when fatigue becomes severe enough to impair reaction time

explanations.a: The manual's recommended break interval is longer than 50 miles or 1 hour.
explanations.b: 250 miles or 5 hours is much longer than the manual's stated guideline.
explanations.c: The manual recommends taking periodic breaks about every 100 miles or 2 hours during long trips to maintain alertness.
explanations.d: Waiting until fatigue is severe is the opposite of the manual's preventive guidance.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.18 Staying alert and fit to drive
questions.text: The CDL manual identifies a single safe response when a driver becomes seriously drowsy on the road. Which option matches the manual's instruction?

answers.text: Drink several cups of strong coffee to stay awake until destination
Open the windows and turn on loud music to fight off drowsiness
Continue driving until the next regularly scheduled stop, regardless of distance
Stop at the nearest safe place and get sleep, because the only safe cure for drowsiness is sleep

explanations.a: The manual notes that caffeine wears off and is not a substitute for sleep.
explanations.b: Loud music and cold air may briefly mask drowsiness but do not address the underlying need for sleep.
explanations.c: Pushing through to a scheduled stop while seriously drowsy is dangerous; the manual instructs drivers to stop at the nearest safe place.
explanations.d: The manual states the only safe cure for drowsiness is sleep, and instructs drivers to stop at the nearest safe place when they realize they are seriously drowsy.

questions.name: Driving Safely and On-Road Operation
questions.objective: 2.18 Staying alert and fit to drive
questions.text: The CDL manual cites several specific risk factors for fall-asleep crashes. Which figure matches the manual's published estimates for adult sleep needs and the increased crash risk associated with working over 60 hours per week?

answers.text: Adults need 8 to 9 hours of sleep, and working more than 60 hours a week increases crash risk by about 40 percent
Adults need 4 to 5 hours of sleep, and working more than 60 hours a week increases crash risk by about 5 percent
Adults need 12 hours of sleep, and working more than 60 hours a week reduces crash risk by 10 percent
Adults need 6 hours of sleep, and working hours have no measurable effect on crash risk

explanations.a: The manual states adults need 8 to 9 hours of sleep to maintain alertness and that working more than 60 hours a week increases the risk of fall-asleep crashes by 40 percent.
explanations.b: 4 to 5 hours is well below the manual's stated requirement and a 5-percent increase understates the published risk figure.
explanations.c: Twelve hours overstates adult sleep needs, and working more does not reduce crash risk.
explanations.d: Six hours understates the manual's recommended sleep, and working hours do affect crash risk.
